region_locator_basis: All names share a regional gateway on this atlas. This point is not any ring's initial separation position, center, or trajectory.
evidence_limit: Horizon publishes no individual positions in its name table, so all names retain one Gulf regional gateway. Separately published positions are point evidence only, and secondary names have no independent separation dates. A source-labeled observational map and an inferred NASA crop seek on the same date do not establish matching eddy identities. Source-event date overlap with NASA model years or an inferred crop date window does not establish a NASA model identity, a visible ring, or an OSW state intersection or containment.

published_observed_position.period: 2024 MASTR discussion; exact center date not stated in cited passage
published_observed_position.source_citation: DiMarco et al., Marine Technology Society Journal 59(3), 2025, Figure 3 discussion
published_observed_position.note: The authors locate the center of rotation of Eddy Berek near 26°N, 89°W. They also describe separation and reattachment from mid-2023 into early 2024. The coordinate is approximate and supplies neither a closed ring footprint nor a NASA model identity.

published_dated_map_presence.source_citation: Bower, Furey, and UGOS Scientific Team, 2024 annual meeting poster, Gulf of Mexico SSH map
published_dated_map_presence.note: The poster labels Eddy Berek on a satellite-derived sea-surface-height map dated 21 December 2023. Its map does not publish a numeric Berek center coordinate, a digitized closed contour, or a NASA ECCO identity.
